name: Tharnariun's Hope
summary: In Auberdine, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turn. Travelers have put down infected beasts across Darkshore, and now he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of town.

sections.title: A Tragic Necessity
sections.body: Since the Third War, an unnatural sickness has made Darkshore's wild creatures rabid. Tharnariun Treetender is stationed in Auberdine, where he has asked travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. Yet killing rabid thistle bears treats only a symptom. Tharnariun decides the source among the local bears must be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother.

sections.title: The Den Mother
sections.body: The Den Mother lurks in a cavern northeast of Auberdine, near the ancient ruins of Bashal'Aran. Once a guardian of the woodland fauna, she was consumed by the affliction spreading across northern Kalimdor. She kept bearing and raising litters of rabid cubs. Alliance heroes hunted her down in her den, ending her torment and stemming the tide of frenzied bears prowling the coastal highway.

sections.title: The Grim Reality of Kalimdor
sections.body: Tharnariun gives profound thanks after the Den Mother's death, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agony. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. Auberdine's defenders accept the heavy burden of protecting their wilderness.

faq.answer: Tharnariun Treetender is a night elf caretaker stationed in Auberdine. Distraught by the blight and madness warping Darkshore's wildlife, he oversees efforts to study and track the suffering animals, then put them out of their misery.

faq.q: Where is the Den Mother located?
faq.answer: The Den Mother dwells in a cave in the hills northeast of Auberdine, just east of the ruins of Bashal'Aran.

faq.q: Why must the Den Mother be killed instead of cured?
faq.answer: The affliction ravaging Darkshore's wildlife grips the beasts and drives them into violent frenzies. With no immediate cure and the Den Mother raising rabid offspring, Tharnariun decides killing her is the only way to stop the sickness from spreading further.

faq.q: What quests lead up to Tharnariun's Hope?
faq.answer: Three parts lead to Tharnariun's Hope. The chain begins with 'Plagued Lands', continues through 'Cleansing of the Infected', and ends with 'Tharnariun's Hope'.

faq.q: What is making the animals of Darkshore sick?
aliases: why are bears rabid in darkshore
faq.answer: Tharnariun names no source. He knows only that a sickness is spreading across Darkshore, gripping the minds and bodies of those it touches. Thistle bears have been hit hardest.

faq.q: Why does Tharnariun mention people escaping to fortified lands?
faq.answer: Auberdine is an exposed coastal outpost beset by ghosts, corrupted wildlife, and hostile creatures. Night elf civilization struggles to rebuild after the Burning Legion's invasion, and some residents feel overwhelmed and hide or retreat toward safer Alliance bastions.

angles.text: For night elves, slaying woodland beasts, especially a matriarch bear, violates their deep reverence for nature. This duty is bitter and sorrowful.
As a druid, you hold bears in high spiritual esteem through the teachings of Ursoc. Killing a corrupted Den Mother reminds you of nature's delicate balance and the tragedies of corruption.
As a hunter, you understand the tragedy of an apex predator driven mad by disease. You know culling an infected beast can be the truest act of mercy.
As an Alliance member, you help protect Auberdine and strengthen the Alliance's foothold along northern Kalimdor's coast. You defend night elf lands from growing wilderness threats.
